kind.description: field for a field of the decision record, form for a form of a structured answer, line for a line an answer is written in, normalization for a step of normalizing an answer, limit for a limit on a decision or an answer, act for what a need asks a person to do, class for a decision class Jig knows, station-key for a kind of need the dispatcher frames, and station-option for an option the dispatcher carries out.

name.description: A field's path in the record (a field of each option as call.options[].<field>), a form's or a line's opening word, a step's or a limit's name, an act or a class as a record names it, the key an answer to a dispatcher's framing names, or an option's id.

type.description: For a field, the JSON type of its value (string, boolean, object, string[] or object[] for a list of strings or objects); null otherwise.

carried.description: For a field, always when every record (or every entry of the list it is in) carries it, sometimes when only some do; null otherwise.

written.description: For a form or a line, how a person writes it, its parts in angle brackets; null otherwise.

step.description: For a normalization step, its place in the order the steps apply, from 1; null otherwise.

value.description: For a limit, its value in its unit; null otherwise.

unit.description: For a limit, what its value counts; null otherwise.

act.description: For a class, the act a decision under it asks for; null otherwise.

class.description: For a station key, the class of the decision the dispatcher frames for it; null otherwise.

options.description: For a station key, the ids of the options its decision offers, in their order, each separated from the next by a comma and a space; null otherwise.

option.description: For a station option, its name as the decision gives it and `choose` names it; null otherwise.

reversible.description: For a station option, true when the decision marks what it does as one that can be undone; null when the decision does not say, and for every other value.

meaning.description: What the value means to a reader that meets it; for a station option, what choosing it does, as the decision's summary says.

values.name: schema
values.meaning: Always `parked-decision/v1`: a reader that meets another value does not read the record as a decision.

values.name: class
values.meaning: The decision class the decision falls in: a class of the repository's human-in-the-loop registry, or one of the dispatcher's own framings. Its act is in the classes table below; a class that table does not list asks a person to decide.

values.name: call
values.meaning: The question, its options and the recommended option.

values.name: call.id
values.meaning: The call's id: one to eight letters or digits.

values.name: call.question
values.meaning: The question a person answers: one line, ending with `?`.

values.name: call.options
values.meaning: The options a person chooses from, at least two, in the order the decision gives them. A refusal or a wait is an option of its own.

values.name: call.options[].id
values.meaning: The option's id, one to eight letters or digits, unique within the call: `call.recommended` names an option by it.

values.name: call.options[].name
values.meaning: The option's name on one line: what `choose <option>` names. No two options' names are the same once normalized, so a `choose` never names two options.

values.name: call.options[].summary
values.meaning: What choosing the option changes.

values.name: call.options[].pay
values.meaning: What choosing the option costs, at least one entry.

values.name: call.options[].tag
values.meaning: A short label shown with the option.

values.name: call.options[].keep
values.meaning: What the option keeps as it is.

values.name: call.options[].rightWhen
values.meaning: When the option is the right one.

values.name: call.options[].obligation
values.meaning: What choosing the option obliges someone to do afterwards.

values.name: call.options[].reversible
values.meaning: Whether what the option does can be undone. A card asks for a second step before it commits a pick of an option marked `false`.

values.name: call.recommended
values.meaning: The id of the option the decision recommends: the option `approve` chooses.

values.name: call.why
values.meaning: Why the decision recommends that option.

values.name: steps
values.meaning: What a person must do by hand whichever option is chosen; empty when there is nothing.

values.name: alreadyDone
values.meaning: What the session that framed the decision already did about it.

values.name: facts
values.meaning: Facts the decision rests on, each with where it was found.

values.name: facts[].text
values.meaning: The fact.

values.name: facts[].source
values.meaning: Where the fact was found: a file and line, a link, a command.

values.name: interplay
values.meaning: How this decision bears on others, entry by entry: what settling one means for another.

values.name: interplay[].from
values.meaning: What the entry starts from, in free text: a call's id, another decision, an issue or a decision record.

values.name: interplay[].to
values.meaning: What the entry bears on, in the same free text as `from`.

values.name: interplay[].text
values.meaning: How the one shrinks or sharpens the other.

values.name: sheet
values.meaning: The address of a decision sheet that sets the decision out at length: an https URL.

values.name: approve
values.meaning: Chooses the option the decision recommends. On a decision that recommends no option it is a free answer.

values.name: choose
values.meaning: Chooses the option whose normalized name is `<option>`. A name no option of the decision has makes it a free answer.

values.name: answer
values.meaning: Answers the decision parked under `<key>` with `<text>`: a structured answer when the comment holds nothing but answer and note lines (and blank lines, `jig send`'s record and quotes of the notification), and the text is one of the forms; otherwise a free answer.

values.name: note
values.meaning: Adds the person's own words to the structured answer to `<key>` beside it, which may narrow the option chosen or set a condition on it, never widen it. A note with no answer beside it answers nothing.

values.name: compatibility
values.meaning: Applies Unicode's compatibility normalization (NFKC): full-width letters and other compatibility forms become their plain forms.

values.name: case
values.meaning: Folds every letter to lower case.

values.name: quotes
values.meaning: Turns typographic single quotes (U+2018 to U+201B) into `'` and double quotes (U+201C to U+201F) into `"`.

values.name: dashes
values.meaning: Turns hyphens and dashes (U+2010 to U+2015) and the minus sign (U+2212) into `-`.

values.name: marks
values.meaning: Removes backticks and the bold marks `**` and `__`, which a pasted or formatted answer may carry.

values.name: white-space
values.meaning: Reads every run of white space as one space, and drops white space at either end.

values.name: final-stop
values.meaning: Drops one full stop or exclamation mark at the end, which a phone's keyboard may add, and the space before it.

values.name: answer-text
values.meaning: The longest an answer's or a note's text may be. A longer one, or one with a line break, another control character or a hidden marker (`<!--`), is not a structured answer, and `jig send` refuses to send it.

values.name: digest
values.meaning: The length of a decision digest: the first characters of the SHA-256 of the decision record as stored, in canonical JSON, kept with the decision. An answer ends with its framing's digest in square brackets, `approve [3fa9c2d1e0b4]`; an answer naming another digest is stale and settles nothing, and one naming none is bound by its time alone.

values.name: decision-bytes
values.meaning: The largest a decision record may be, as UTF-8 JSON. A park, a dispatched session's result and its closing report refuse a larger one.

values.name: Merge
values.meaning: Merge the pull request: only a person merges.

values.name: Decide
values.meaning: Choose among the options the decision frames.

values.name: Authorize
values.meaning: Allow, or refuse, what only a person may allow; refusing is an option of the decision's own.

values.name: Reply
values.meaning: Answer a person's review thread.

values.name: Do
values.meaning: Perform steps by hand, outside the line.

values.name: Investigate
values.meaning: Look into what went wrong: a failure or a stall nobody framed as a decision.

values.name: scope
values.meaning: Expand a pull request's scope.

values.name: next-item
values.meaning: Pick the next item from the computed ranking.

values.name: reopen-or-waive
values.meaning: Reopen an item on a rejecting verdict, or waive a missing acceptance review.

values.name: escalated
values.meaning: A review thread the review arbiter escalated with no recorded person's decision behind it.

values.name: human-decision
values.meaning: A fix that would change what the pull request records as a person's decision, or a decision only a person can take; a pass that cannot read the repository's policy parks every decision under it.

values.name: merge
values.meaning: Merge a pull request.

values.name: ready
values.meaning: Mark a pull request ready for review.

values.name: release
values.meaning: Release or promote to production.

values.name: destructive
values.meaning: A destructive operation: data loss or a history rewrite.

values.name: legal
values.meaning: A legal or data-protection sign-off.

values.name: copy
values.meaning: Publish customer-facing copy.

values.name: dark-dial
values.meaning: Flip a dial that is off by default.

values.name: rules
values.meaning: Change the rules the agents follow: instructions and scaffolding.

values.name: reviewer-posture
values.meaning: Promote an automated reviewer to blocking, or waive a failing advisory check.

values.name: human-thread
values.meaning: A person's review thread an agent may not overrule on its own, or a person's reversal of a provisional decision.

values.name: followup-recovery
values.meaning: The dispatcher's framing: how a follow-up that failed or whose claim went stale goes on.

values.name: pickup-recovery
values.meaning: The dispatcher's framing: how a pickup that stalled, stopped on a question or ended without moving its item goes on.

values.name: checkout-recovery
values.meaning: The dispatcher's framing: how a checkout another tree holds is freed for a launch.

values.name: drive-recovery
values.meaning: The dispatcher's framing: how a drive that handed its pull request to a person goes on.

values.name: launch-recovery
values.meaning: The dispatcher's framing: how a launch record no tick launches again is settled.

values.name: followup
values.meaning: A merged pull request's follow-up whose pass ended without recording done, or whose claim no session is joined to.

values.name: release
values.meaning: One untagged release, answered on its tracker item.

values.name: pickup
values.meaning: A pickup that stalled, stopped on a question it did not frame, or ended without moving its item on.

values.name: checkout
values.meaning: A launch that waits because a checkout the workspace runtime does not list holds its branch and is in use.

values.name: drive
values.meaning: A drive that stopped and handed its pull request to a person.

values.name: launch
values.meaning: A pending launch record that no tick launches again.

values.name: rerun
values.meaning: The dispatcher releases the follow-up's claim (its marker comment), and a later tick starts the follow-up again once, with your note, when you add one, as a person's answer in its prompt.

values.name: done
values.meaning: The dispatcher marks the follow-up's marker done and sets the pull request's followed-up label; nothing runs again.

values.name: release
values.meaning: The dispatcher moves the item back to the state a pickup starts from, so a later tick picks it up afresh in a new session.

values.name: detach
values.meaning: The dispatcher detaches the checkout from its branch (its files and commits stay where they are), so the launch can take the branch.

values.name: rearm
values.meaning: The dispatcher re-arms the drive once on the pull request's current head, as the rearm label does.

values.name: clear
values.meaning: The dispatcher clears the stuck launch record, as jig dispatch clear does, which frees its slot; a later tick may start its stage again.

values.name: gates
values.meaning: The dispatcher requests another run of the failed jobs on the releasing commit once.

values.name: inspect
values.meaning: Take the tracker item and determine what is holding back the tag.

values.name: tag
values.meaning: Take the tracker item and create the tag by hand after checking it is safe to release.

values.name: hold
values.option: I'll handle it — hide this card
values.meaning: Nothing is done; the work stays where it is. The dispatcher hides this card for these facts and lists it again when they change.
